description:
## Outcome

The coding pack supplies replaceable structured Git status and diff tools plus trusted named verification helpers for tests and lint.

## Why now

Coding users need to inspect changes and verify them. These features can now reuse read, shell, policy, workspace, and evidence contracts.

## Current state

No Git or verification tools exist. The future write/edit tool returns edit records, and the shell tool can run bounded commands. Raw model-selected test commands would be unsafe and nonportable.

## Ownership and boundary

This is a `jidoka` built-in extension change. Git and helper commands run through the constrained shell/environment. Trusted host configuration defines helper IDs and command templates. The model can select a helper and safe parameters, not an arbitrary configured command.

## Detailed implementation

1. Register `coding.git_status` and `coding.git_diff` with structured, bounded outputs.
2. Restrict Git work to the trusted workspace and path filters. Report non-repository state, staged/unstaged/untracked facts, renames, binary files, and truncation.
3. Define named verification helper data with ID, description, fixed command template, allowed target parameters, timeout, network need, and expected exit policy.
4. Register one general `coding.verify` operation that selects only a trusted helper ID.
5. Run all commands through constrained shell and policy. Return separate output, exit facts, confirmed evidence, and linked edit/checkpoint IDs where supplied.
6. Allow each Git tool and helper to be disabled or replaced.
7. Keep results portable and deterministic in ordering.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Git status and diff return stable structured results for clean and dirty repositories.
- [ ] Path filters, ignore rules, binary files, and output limits are enforced.
- [ ] A named test/lint helper runs its trusted template only.
- [ ] Unknown helper or unsafe target fails before shell execution.
- [ ] Git unavailable, non-repository, nonzero helper, timeout, and cancellation have distinct results.
- [ ] No helper command comes from agent or scenario data.

## Test plan

- Success: clean/dirty Git repo, staged/unstaged/untracked changes, bounded diff, passing test and lint helpers.
- Invalid input: outside-root path, unknown helper, invalid target, and oversized diff request.
- Runtime failure: Git missing, non-repo, nonzero verification, timeout, cancellation, and environment error.
- Boundary and security: helper command injection, network deny, ignored secret path, and weak evidence.
- Deterministic capability: temp Git fixture or fake executor, trusted helper registry, policy, clock, and IDs.
- JSONL and exit status: results Jason-encode with bounded stdout/stderr and confirmed evidence.

## Documentation

Document Git result fields, limits, helper configuration, safe parameter substitution, status meanings, and disable/replace rules.

## Non-goals

Do not commit, push, reset, checkout, or modify Git state. Do not add arbitrary workflow files, CI integration, or background commands.

## Dependencies

Blocking issues:

- `jido_cli-tqg.5.2` — Add removable read and search coding tools
- `jido_cli-tqg.5.4` — Add a bounded constrained shell tool

Features unlocked by this story:

- CLI edit review
- Default test and lint workflows
- Clear post-change evidence

## Commit plan

Create exactly one focused `jidoka` commit. Use a message such as `feat(jidoka): add coding review and verification tools (jido_cli-tqg.5.5)`. Do not include another backlog feature.

## Verification commands

```sh
cd /Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_cli/jidoka
mix test test/jidoka/coding_pack/git_test.exs test/jidoka/coding_pack/verify_test.exs test/integration/coding_pack_git_integration_test.exs
mix quality
mix test
mix docs
```
title: Add Git review tools and named verification helpers
